description: Ontology for assessing whether electronic-device faults are software-side, hardware-side, or located on the hardware/software boundary.

boundary_types.name: Software-side fault
boundary_types.definition: The evidence is dominated by driver, operating-system, configuration, data, or filesystem context without confirmatory hardware failure evidence.

boundary_types.name: Hardware-side fault
boundary_types.definition: The evidence is dominated by hardware health, device-state, SMART/WHEA, or active-test failure signals.

boundary_types.name: Hardware/software boundary fault
boundary_types.definition: The evidence spans software or firmware control and physical hardware or interface-path signals, so software stack and hardware endpoint must be isolated before service action.

boundary_types.name: Mixed or uncertain boundary
boundary_types.definition: Evidence is insufficient, contradictory, or only symptom-level, so boundary attribution is not reliable.

active_boundary_tests.purpose: Separate driver/OS crash context from WHEA, storage, memory, or board-level evidence.
Separate adapter/battery/connector faults from ACPI, UCSI, firmware, and power-policy faults.
Separate display panel/backlight/path faults from display driver and boot-state faults.
Separate WLAN hardware, driver, OS network stack, router, and external environment faults.
